raw_response:
I’m an old hand at this, so I won’t do anything fancy. On my 8.5 mu, I’ll keep doing what feels steady and safe for the family. Sunflower is my main crop, because it’s easier to manage on its own and doesn’t need me running around too much. But I still want some wheat and maize on part of the land, because if one side does poorly, the other can still bring something back. With people in the house working off-farm, labor at home is not enough for too much fine management, so I’ll keep the plan simple, use the well when the crop really needs it, and not spend too much cash at once.

For the 5 mu sunflower, I’ll use the same local or improved seed I can get nearby, sow in late April, put some base fertilizer before planting, and if the plants look weak later I’ll add a little more. Sunflower doesn’t need as much water as wheat, so I’ll irrigate once or twice depending on rain. On the other 3.5 mu, I’ll do wheat first, then maize after harvest. Wheat still matters because we’ve grown it many years and I trust it. I’ll feed it a bit more than sunflower, and give it a few well-waterings because wheat without water is hard to watch. After wheat comes off, I’ll hurry and plant maize right away. The turnaround is tight, so I won’t do heavy tillage there, just quick land prep and sow. I won’t chase very high yield this year. Better to spend within my means and get a stable harvest.
